commit_message:
dtls: buffer early CCS to handle UDP reorder

Cache early-arriving CCS in dtls1_state_st and replay it when the
handshake reaches the expected state. Clear the flag in
dtls1_clear_received_buffer().

Add dtls_ccs_reorder_test covering client/server reorder, resumption and mutual TLS.

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.foundation>
MergeDate: Mon Mar 16 11:01:55 2026
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/30225)

fix_commit.message: Fix a Use-After-Free bug in the DTLS code
fix_commit.author: Matt Caswell

findings.title: Use-after-free when buffering early CCS in DTLS
findings.message: The CCS buffering mechanism for UDP reorder tolerance does not account for trailing data in the current record buffer. When an early-arriving CCS is buffered using `has_change_cipher_spec = 1` and `goto redo`, the code continues processing. Later, when the buffered CCS is delivered (when `dtls_ccs_expected()` returns true), it triggers `tls_process_change_cipher_spec()` -> `ssl3_do_change_cipher_spec()` -> `tls1_change_cipher_state()` -> `ssl_set_new_record_layer()`, which frees the old record layer buffer via `dtls_free()` -> `tls_free()` -> `tls_int_free()` -> `ossl_tls_buffer_release()`. However, if there is trailing data left in the current record at the point of the cipher change, the pointers to that buffer become dangling. Subsequent reads via `dtls1_read_bytes()` access freed memory, causing a heap-use-after-free.
findings.suggestion: Before switching to a new record layer epoch, verify that all trailing record data has been consumed. If trailing data exists when attempting to change cipher state in DTLS, either process it first or return an error. The fix adds a check in ssl_set_new_record_layer() that returns SSL_AD_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE if s->rlayer.curr_rec < s->rlayer.num_recs for DTLS connections.

ground_truth.root_cause: The CCS buffering mechanism using `has_change_cipher_spec = 1` and `goto redo` does not verify that all data in the current record buffer has been consumed before allowing a cipher state change. When the buffered CCS triggers ssl_set_new_record_layer(), the old buffer is freed, but dangling pointers to trailing data in that buffer remain, leading to use-after-free on subsequent reads.
